open_obligations: Note that Goel et al. study correctness grading, not choosing between debaters.
Check whether using distinct LLMs, as Liang et al. recommend, removes the similarity effect Goel et al. find across families.
Check the partial-correlation controls for accuracy.
out.other_title: MAD limitations: time cost, long-context failures, judge self-preference
out.rationale: Liang et al. state an LLM judge may prefer its own outputs and recommend same-LLM or distinct-LLM setups. Goel et al. report an average Pearson r = 0.84 between judge scores and judge-model similarity across 9 judges, extending beyond self- or family-preference; their judges grade free-text answers for correctness, not debate sides.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether LLM judges prefer outputs from themselves or similar models, for LLM-as-a-judge on MMLU-Pro

text: The paper reports that, for example, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as judge scores Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as 71% correct but the more capable Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (51% vs 41% MCQ accuracy) as 67%, and finds a significant (p < 0.01) positive correlation, average Pearson r = 0.84, between LLM-as-a-judge scores and judge-model similarity (kappa_p) for all judges, extending beyond self- or family-preference.
title: LLM judges favour functionally similar models (affinity bias), average r = 0.84
